title: CmdPal: Failing event handler blocks extension updates

linked_refs.title: CmdPal: Prevent failing event handlers from blocking updates

actions.label: Link active CmdPal fix PR
actions.note: Draft a maintainer note that points the issue to the active upstream PR.

comment.body: This report already has active upstream engineering coverage in PR 50485 (`CmdPal: Prevent failing event handlers from blocking updates`). The proposed change matches the failing path described here: it isolates each notification subscriber so one extension-side failure does not block later list or dock listeners, and it removes disconnected RPC handlers from the invocation list. I would avoid parallel design work and track this issue against that PR instead.

issue_context.summary: A Command Palette extension can stay responsive while later list or dock updates go stale if one notification subscriber throws and blocks the rest of the dispatch fan-out.
known_information: The issue was opened from main/dev-build context and is already assigned to jiripolasek.
A same-day linked PR, 50485, says it handles per-subscriber failures separately and removes disconnected RPC handlers.

The current SDK still calls PropChanged and ItemsChanged through shared delegates in src/modules/cmdpal/extensionsdk/Microsoft.CommandPalette.Extensions.Toolkit/BaseObservable.cs, ContentPage.cs, and CommandProvider.cs.
inferences: The stale-list/stale-dock symptom is most consistent with one failing subscriber aborting the shared event invocation chain before later listeners run.
Because an upstream PR already targets that exact dispatch path, additional dashboard design work would likely duplicate live owner work.
issue_context.analysis: This is handled rather than missing-triage work. The current code shape matches the report, but the active upstream PR already captures the intended remediation: isolate per-subscriber failures and prune dead handlers so later subscribers still receive update notifications.
initial_investigation: src/modules/cmdpal/extensionsdk/Microsoft.CommandPalette.Extensions.Toolkit/BaseObservable.cs invokes PropChanged directly inside a try/catch, which hides failures but does not isolate individual subscribers.
src/modules/cmdpal/extensionsdk/Microsoft.CommandPalette.Extensions.Toolkit/ContentPage.cs and CommandProvider.cs do the same for ItemsChanged.
PR 50485 is open at https://github.com/microsoft/PowerToys/pull/50485 with a title and summary that explicitly match this issue.

judgment.rationale: The issue already has an active upstream fix attempt: PR 50485 explicitly closes this report and targets the failing-notification path in the Command Palette extension SDK.
evidence: Issue 50483 is assigned to jiripolasek and cross-references PR 50485.
PR 50485 says it dispatches property and item notifications independently per subscriber so one failure does not block later listeners.

The current SDK raises PropChanged and ItemsChanged directly from shared delegates in BaseObservable.cs, ContentPage.cs, and CommandProvider.cs, matching the reported failure mode where one bad handler can block later subscribers.
judgment.recommended_action: Point maintainers to PR 50485 instead of opening parallel design work.

fix_assessment.rationale: A public upstream pull request is already open for the exact failing notification-dispatch path.
